messages:
li: Heads-up from the nightly load: after kernel-selector tweak we see host-side ingress costs rising, mainly in tokenization + HTTP/2 frame handling. p99 latency on small requests jumped ~15%.

andre: Which tweak? The one that prefers micro-kernels for sequences < 40?

li: Yep. kernel-selector 3.2 changed small-seq cutoff 32->40 and prefers micro-kernel paths that disable some batch coalescing. That made avg_batch_size fall from 9.2 -> 5.6 for our small-inference traffic.

maria: Quick profile summary from the repro cluster (50k reqs):
```
29.4%  host::tokenizer::utf8_scan
21.7%  http2::frame_reader::parse
12.9%  host::preparse::memmove_loop
7.8%   runtime::kvcache::get_missing
```
writev/syscall churn up ~3.4x on smallwrite traces.

andre: Ouch. The memmove_loop looks like we're copying frames per-request instead of coalescing. Did we change frame handling for micro-kernel mode?

li: There was an optimization that avoided copying the first frame when batchable, but the micro-kernel path disables the batchable flag earlier. So we end up doing more per-request copies.

perf-bot: Regression alert: smallwrite_tail_ratio increased 2.9x at 2026-03-21T04:12:00Z. See perf-suite/alerts/6087654321.

maria: Experiment notes I ran: three branches on a 10% shadow fleet:
- baseline (pre-3.2)
- 3.2 micro-pref -> showed p99 +15%
- 3.2 + frame-coalesce-hotpatch -> p99 +4% (better but not baseline)

andre: What's the frame-coalesce-hotpatch? Pseudo please.

li: Patch logic: when we detect consecutive HEADERS/CONTINUATION frames <= 512B within the same stream and within 2ms, we append them into a single parse buffer and parse once. Pseudo: 
```
if (stream.peek_next_frame().type in {HEADERS, CONTINUATION} &&
    stream.peek_next_frame().len <= 512 &&
    now - stream.last_frame_time <= 2ms) {
  coalesced.reserve(1024);
  while (next_frame && next_frame.len <= 512 && coalesced.len < 2048) {
    coalesced.append(next_frame.payload);
    advance();
  }
  parse_headers(coalesced);
} else {
  parse_headers(next_frame.payload);
}
```
This reduces per-frame state machine calls and fewer memcpy calls.

maria: Microbench: header-parse calls reduced 48%, tokenization CPU down 12% (because we avoid re-entering tokenize per fragment). But the hotpatch adds a small allocation path; using a thread-local scratch buffer keeps alloc overhead negligible.

andre: What about KV cache? Did more small batches increase unique key churn?

li: Yes. kvcache_map_size grew and eviction rate doubled on small workloads. Hit rate fell 0.94 -> 0.86. I tested raising per-shard capacity + extending TTL from 5s -> 12s and got hit rate back to 0.91 on the patch nodes.

maria: Combined numbers from the 10% shadow run (10k small requests):
```
baseline:    p99=180ms, p50=22ms, kvcache_hit=0.94
3.2:         p99=207ms, p50=23ms, kvcache_hit=0.86
3.2+hotfix:  p99=188ms, p50=23ms, kvcache_hit=0.91
```
So hotfix recovers most of the tail and kvcache tweak helps.

andre: Good. Longer-term we should make kernel-selector aware of host-cost signals (e.g., predicted host_cpu_cost) so it doesn't blindly prefer micro-kernels when host overhead wins out.

li: Agreed. Short-term rollout plan:
1) push frame-coalesce-hotpatch to 20% canary (no config change)
2) apply kvcache per-shard bump to canary nodes (config deploy)
3) revert micro-pref cutoff change in kernel-selector until we can instrument host-cost in the decision.

maria: Also adding a perf-suite replay that stresses small token counts (median 5 tokens) + measures writev rate and kvcache eviction. I'll add an automated flamegraph snapshot step to nightly canary runs for kernel-selector rollouts.

perf-bot: Job queued: perf-suite/replays/small-requests -> run at 2026-03-21T06:00:00Z.

andre: One more micro-opt: reuse per-thread header scratch and avoid memcpy by parsing from the input ringbuffer when contiguous. Could save another ~6-8% CPU. But need careful lifetime handling.

li: I'll prototype that after the coalesce landing. Action items: li (hotfix + prototype scratch reuse), maria (perf replay + flamegraph snapshot), andre (kernel-selector host-cost spec).
